name: no-embedded-template-assets
body: The kalide binary's embedded content is exactly the core of the tool: the vendored reveal.js runtime, the deck/error/gallery page shells, the minimal `kalide init` seed tree (written to disk by the no-arg `kalide init` and refreshable in place by `kalide upgrade`, requirements.requirement.upgrade-refresh-owned-scaffold), the static, text-only author-guide files (requirements.requirement.agent-authoring) — the deck-author full guide `AGENTS_KALIDE.md` and its short `AGENTS.md` pointer written by `kalide init` and `kalide init <path>`, and the library/template-author full guide and pointer written by `kalide init-library` (agent-guide-reference) — and the scaffold-version digest catalog (global.constraint.upgrade-known-version-catalog): the identity/version metadata and content digests of the released kalide-owned scaffold files, core upgrade metadata that carries no file contents and no presentation assets. Every template, theme and media file used for validating, rendering, listing or serving a deck is read at run time from the resolved library layers — the external library at the configured `templates:` path in `kalide.yaml` when set, and the deck-root `templates/` directory when it exists (see layered-template-library). The binary holds no templates, themes, fonts, logos or other presentation media (images, video, …), and there is no built-in fallback: a layer that lacks something is an error. The vendored runtime and page shells are core, not template assets; the scaffold guide files are scaffold content, not template assets, and are never referenced as one. The seed tree and the guide files are written to disk by the scaffolding commands and may be rewritten in place by `kalide upgrade` only when the target file is byte-identical to a catalogued released version — or, for the full guide `AGENTS_KALIDE.md` only, when it is absent, and for the `AGENTS.md` pointer, per the reference rule (global.constraint.upgrade-never-clobbers); the catalog is core upgrade metadata — digests and version metadata, never historical file contents and never presentation assets. None of the embedded content carries a brand (global.constraint.core-unbranded).
